mechanics.name: Royal Exchanges
unlock: Available from the start (Reincarnation 0): the Royal Market opens as soon as you have chosen a faction.

sections.title: What they are
sections.text: Royal Exchanges are bought in the Royal Market with Faction Coins, one coin type per faction. Every exchange you buy adds to a bonus that multiplies all of your production. An exchange can be bought any number of times, and the price rises with every one you buy of the same coin type.

sections.title: Bonus per exchange
sections.text: By default every exchange is worth 10%. This is the Individual Bonus shown in the Royal Market. It does not depend on how many exchanges you have bought or on your Ascension; only upgrades, researches and similar items change it. Some add a flat amount, some add an amount that grows with a stat of yours, and some multiply the result.

sections.title: Overall bonus
sections.text: The overall bonus multiplies your total production. With no exchanges bought it is 1. At Ascension 0 every exchange adds b% of your production: 100 exchanges at 10% give a multiplier of 11. From Ascension 1 the Ascension penalty below applies.

sections.title: Ascension penalty
sections.text: From Ascension 1 the overall bonus is raised to a power p that is below 1 instead of being used as it is. This is not the penalty of the researches (the A marks): the exchanges have their own formula, which weakens with every Ascension. The Individual Bonus shown in the Royal Market is not reduced, only the overall bonus is.

sections.title: Cost
sections.text: The first exchange of a coin type costs 20 Faction Coins of that type. Each one you buy of that coin type makes the next one g times as expensive, so the price of the next one is about 20 · g to the power of the number already bought. Every coin type has its own count. The formula gives the total price of buying k more when n are already bought; g is called the cost multiplier and starts at 1.1.
